stories.title: Shidika Goode helps students navigate Penn State
stories.summary: Shidika Goode arrived at Penn State in 2009 with ambitions of becoming a veterinarian. As a first-generation student, she found the transition to campus life difficult. She now works to make the university experience easier for students who find themselves in similar positions.

stories.title: Punjab government offers free civil services coaching
stories.summary: The Punjab government will provide free online coaching for UPSC and Punjab Civil Services examinations to 1,000 college students. The program, spearheaded by Education Minister Harjot Bains, will cover 750 students from government colleges and 250 from private colleges. The government aims to make preparation more accessible.

stories.title: Indian Bank invites applications for 1,500 apprentice posts
stories.summary: Indian Bank has invited applications for 1,500 training vacancies under the Apprentices Act. The recruitment is open to graduates, with the process running from November 5 to November 25. Selection involves an online examination and a local language proficiency test. The bank has released full eligibility details online.

stories.title: UPSC declares Civil Services Mains 2026 results
stories.summary: The Union Public Service Commission has declared the results for the Civil Services Mains 2026. A total of 2,526 candidates have qualified for the personality test, which serves as the final stage of the selection process. The written examination was conducted in August.

stories.title: Odisha Police announces 7,268 vacancies
stories.summary: The Odisha Uniformed Services Staff Selection Commission has released a notification for 7,268 vacancies across constable, firefighter, driver and traffic constable positions. The application process began on October 23 and remains open until November 12. The commission published the details under Advertisement Number 01-CRE-2026.

stories.title: PGIMER postpones Nursing Officer examination
stories.summary: The Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research has released admit cards for 243 nursing officer vacancies. The computer-based test, originally scheduled for October 21, has been moved to November 18. Candidates can download their hall tickets from the institute website.

stories.title: UPSC opens portal for interview form updates
stories.summary: Following the release of the Civil Services Mains 2026 results, the Union Public Service Commission has announced that successful candidates must update their application forms. The portal will be open for these updates from November 11 to November 25. A total of 2,526 candidates qualified for interviews.

stories.title: UPSC declares final NDA and NA results
stories.summary: The Union Public Service Commission has announced the final results for the National Defence Academy and Naval Academy Examination. A total of 617 candidates have qualified for admission to the Army, Navy and Air Force wings. The list follows written exams and Ministry of Defence interviews.

stories.title: IX-WAI offers early career grants for women in AI
stories.summary: The I-X Women in AI Network is accepting applications for its 2027 Early Career Development Grant. The program provides up to 1,000 pounds to women and non-binary individuals working in or entering the field of AI. The deadline for applications is January 4, 2027.

stories.title: Uttar Pradesh relaxes graduation requirements for teachers
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has relaxed the minimum graduation marks requirement for assistant teacher candidates. The change applies to those admitted to teacher education programs before July 29, 2011. The amendment aims to address eligibility issues for candidates who previously failed to meet the prescribed percentage.

stories.title: West Bengal Public Service Commission releases WBCS prelims results
stories.summary: The West Bengal Public Service Commission has declared the results for the 2024 preliminary examination. A total of 3,842 candidates have been provisionally shortlisted for the main examination. The commission published the merit list in PDF format on its official website.

stories.title: UPSC CSE Mains scorecards expected this month
stories.summary: The Union Public Service Commission is expected to release the Civil Services Examination Mains results in November. While no official date is set, the commission typically publishes results 70 to 75 days after the examination concludes. Candidates can check the official website for updates.

stories.title: Tanvi Patri finds success after badminton training in China
stories.summary: Tanvi Patri, 15, recently won a silver medal at the Youth Olympics. Her training began in China, where her father also received coaching alongside her. Five years after returning to India, she is now competing on the international stage.

stories.title: Mysuru student wins district-level Yoga Olympiad
stories.summary: K. Pavan, a student at Karnataka Public School, secured first place in the Mysuru district-level Yoga Olympiad. He has been selected to compete in the state-level event. Local officials and school staff attended the competition to congratulate the winner.

stories.title: Tanvi Patri secures silver at Youth Olympics
stories.summary: Tanvi Patri, 15, became the first Indian woman to win a Youth Olympics badminton silver medal. Despite a comeback attempt in the final, she fell short against China's Zhang Yi Xin. Patri saved five match points before the match concluded in Dakar.

stories.title: Jaypal Malviya secures 2028 Olympic shooting quota
stories.summary: Jaypal Malviya won a silver medal in the men's 10m air pistol event at the ISSF World Championships in Doha. The performance secured India's first shooting quota for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Other Indian competitors did not qualify for individual spots.

stories.title: Maaya Rajeshwaran advances at Chennai Open
stories.summary: Maaya Rajeshwaran remains the final Indian singles hope at the Chennai Open after defeating Poland's Weronika Falkowska. National number one Vaishnavi Adkar was eliminated in the round of 16 by Anastasia Zakharova. Rajeshwaran secured her victory in straight sets.

stories.title: India secures team silver at ISSF World Championships
stories.summary: India secured a team silver medal in the women's 10m air pistol event at the ISSF World Championships. Manu Bhaker and Suruchi Inder Singh failed to secure individual Olympic quotas during the event. The team finished with 1,738 points.

stories.title: St. George students qualify for state-level shooting
stories.summary: Two students from St. George International School in Karimnagar have qualified for state-level SGFI air rifle shooting competitions. N. Suhakshi and N. Vinmayi secured their spots after competing in selection trials at the Swadesh Shooting Sports Academy. The school staff expressed pride in the students' shooting skills.

stories.title: Postgraduate student wins award for space biology proposal
stories.summary: Sanskriti Sanvi, a postgraduate student at Chanakya University, has won a 1 lakh rupee award for her STELLA proposal. The project outlines a multi-stress simulation chamber designed to research how microorganisms respond to space conditions. The Department of Biotechnology announced the results as part of its BioE3 Challenge.

stories.title: ISSO basketball championship concludes in Gurugram
stories.summary: The International Schools Sports Organisation concluded its 2026 National Basketball Championship at The Shri Ram School in Gurugram. The event featured 60 teams from international schools across India. Organisers cited the tournament as a celebration of competitive sport, teamwork and the growing popularity of basketball in international schools.

stories.title: Guwahati college hosts sustainable science conference
stories.summary: B. Borooah College in Guwahati recently concluded a two-day international conference on sustainable science. The event featured 13 technical sessions and 144 research presentations. Participants included scientists and academics from institutions such as Harvard, Stanford and the University of Cambridge. Science was discussed in detail.

stories.title: Gas detection suggests Mars may be geologically active
stories.summary: Researchers have detected hydrogen chloride in the Martian atmosphere above fissures near Alba Mons, suggesting the planet may still have an active interior. The findings, published in Science Advances, challenge the long-held view that Martian volcanic activity belongs to the distant past. The planet is reconsidering its retirement.

stories.title: Engineers adjust to AI-generated code
stories.summary: Three-quarters of all new code at Google is now AI-generated and approved by engineers. Microsoft's CTO predicts this will reach 95 percent within five years. The shift does not eliminate the need for software engineers, but it does change the nature of their work. Someone still checks the output.

stories.title: Educators suggest verbal rehearsal for writing
stories.summary: Tanya Baker of the National Writing Project suggests that having students think out loud can help them overcome writing challenges. Educators say this verbal rehearsal practice works for all students, particularly those struggling to get thoughts on paper. It is used both to start and to refine writing.

stories.title: Project-based learning advocates for public showcases
stories.summary: Educators say project-based learning programs should conclude with public showcases to extend their benefits. Students might apply math to community security or science to water conservation. The approach aims to engage students through practical applications of their studies. The projects are intended to be seen by others.

stories.title: Science Olympiad Foundation releases exam details
stories.summary: The Science Olympiad Foundation held its International Science Olympiad Level 1 exams on October 30. Results and answer keys are expected to be released on the organization's website throughout November and December. Students use these keys to estimate their scores before the Level 2 exams commence.

stories.title: Turkmenistan holds first stage of subject Olympiads
stories.summary: The Institute of International Relations in Turkmenistan has held the first stage of subject Olympiads for 12th-grade students. Approximately 800 students competed in history, mathematics and languages. The event is timed to coincide with International Education Day. The best performers will qualify for a final round.

stories.title: Turkmenistan announces logistics Olympiad for students
stories.summary: The Institute of Telecommunications and Informatics of Turkmenistan is hosting an internet-based logistics Olympiad on November 20. Participation is limited to five students per higher education institution. The event aims to promote initiatives discussed at the recent CICA summit. The internet will be used for the competition.

stories.title: Northwest Technical College celebrates scholarship recipients
stories.summary: Northwest Technical College and its Foundation celebrated 66 scholarship recipients at an annual breakfast on October 29. The college awarded a total of $92,500 to students. The funds were provided by a variety of local organizations, including health foundations, communications firms, and a vintage auto club.

stories.title: Dangote Cement expands scholarship scheme in Kogi
stories.summary: Dangote Cement PLC has awarded scholarships to 75 students from the Oworo community in Kogi State. This brings the company's total scholarship count to 125 for the 2025 to 2026 period. The initiative aims to expand the company's corporate social responsibility footprint beyond its five primary catchment areas.

stories.title: Findlay-Hancock County Foundation awards $440,000 in scholarships
stories.summary: The Findlay-Hancock County Community Foundation awarded $440,000 in scholarships to 284 students in 2026. This latest distribution brings the foundation's 31-year total to more than $7.3 million. The foundation supports students across several Ohio counties, including Hancock, Hardin, and Allen.

stories.title: Shidler College celebrates scholarship funding
stories.summary: The Shidler College of Business at the University of Hawaii recently held an annual event to celebrate the distribution of more than $1.4 million in student scholarships. The event highlighted the financial support provided to students during the current academic year.

stories.title: Type Directors Club awards 2026 scholarships
stories.summary: The Type Directors Club has announced the winners of its three annual global student scholarship programs. Maya Cisneros, a student at the School of Visual Arts, received the $5,000 Adé Hogue Scholarship. The program is designed for BIPOC students demonstrating exceptional promise in design and typography.

stories.title: OLLAS awards record scholarship funds to UNO students
stories.summary: The Office of Latino and Latin American Studies at the University of Nebraska at Omaha awarded $389,634 in scholarships for the 2026 to 2027 academic year. The funds supported 44 students through two specific scholarship programs. The department described the total as a record number for the office.

stories.title: SUNY Canton announces scholarship fundraising drive
stories.summary: SUNY Canton has launched a new initiative to raise $1 million in scholarship support for next fall. The college awarded $840,000 in aid this year, which officials described as the most in its history. The college says it is always moving forward.

stories.title: Indus Towers marks decade of scholarship support
stories.summary: Indus Towers Limited celebrated ten years of its scholarship program by honoring 77 students with disabilities from five Northeastern states. The initiative, run in partnership with Shishu Sarothi, aims to improve access to higher education. The company says it is committed to its flagship corporate social responsibility program.

stories.title: CUHK invests over HK$60 million in scholarships
stories.summary: The Chinese University of Hong Kong has presented its inaugural Fenghuang Scholarship to 81 freshmen. The university also awarded eight Vice-Chancellor’s Scholarships for Excellence. The institution stated it is investing over HK$60 million in top talent to recognize achievements in academics, leadership, and service.

stories.title: Prudential-ACLEDA scholarship program launches in Cambodia
stories.summary: The Prudential-ACLEDA Undergraduate Scholarship Programme has launched to provide financial support to Cambodian students. The full details regarding the program's scope and application process are available for subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Assam opens scholarship applications for 2026 to 2027
stories.summary: Applications for the 2026 to 2027 academic session scholarship schemes for SC and OBC students in Assam are now open. Interested students can access the application portal through the official website. Further details on eligibility and deadlines are available for subscribers.

stories.title: Invercargill Licensing Trust awards tertiary scholarships
stories.summary: The Invercargill Licensing Trust awarded scholarships to 65 recipients at a presentation on November 2. Each student will receive $2,000 annually for three years. The trust also participates in a tertiary preparation program aimed at helping Pacifika students transition into higher education.

stories.title: IIM releases CAT 2026 admit cards
stories.summary: The Indian Institute of Management is releasing hall tickets for the Common Admission Test today. Candidates can download their admit cards from the official website using their application login ID and password. The exam is scheduled to take place later this year.

stories.title: CBSE sets practical exam dates for winter-bound schools
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has released the practical examination schedule for winter-bound schools. Assessments for classes 10 and 12 will take place from November 9 to December 19, 2026. The schedule includes project and internal assessments for the 2026 to 2027 academic session.

stories.title: CBSE releases practical exam schedule for winter-bound schools
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has announced that practical exams for winter-bound schools will run from November 9 to December 19, 2026. A separate schedule for regular schools is expected to begin on January 1, 2027. Schools are instructed to appoint external teachers for the evaluations.

stories.title: CBSE mandates batch photos for practical exams
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has scheduled practical exams for winter-bound schools between November 9 and December 19, 2026. The board has also mandated the use of app-based batch photos and strict adherence to the official list of candidates for all evaluations.

stories.title: CBSE announces practical exam dates for winter-bound schools
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has released the practical exam schedule for winter-bound schools, starting November 9, 2026. Practical exams for regular schools will follow on January 1, 2027. The notification covers project and internal assessments for both class 10 and class 12 students.

stories.title: CBSE issues practical exam dates for winter-bound schools
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has released the practical exam schedule for winter-bound schools for the 2026 to 2027 academic session. Exams will occur from November 9 to December 19, 2026. A separate circular will be issued for schools following the regular academic session.

stories.summary: ON CAMPUS Getting into a prestigious university abroad involves much more than securing good grades. For Pakistani students hoping to study at Ivy League universities in the United States or leading institutions in the United Kingdom, preparation needs to begin well before the application deadline.

stories.title: Federal court dismisses visa lawsuit from Stanford researcher
stories.summary: A federal judge has dismissed a lawsuit from Zhilin Liu, a Stanford doctoral student seeking to resolve a stalled visa renewal. The court ruled it lacks the legal power to intervene in State Department consular processes. The researcher remains in limbo after his application vanished into a black hole.

stories.title: Australia consults on international student visa reforms
stories.summary: The Australian government is seeking feedback on reforms to its Genuine Student test and financial requirements. Assistant Minister for International Education Julian Hill aims to discourage visa hopping and permanent temporary migration. The sector faces these potential changes after a year of record-high visa refusal rates for international students.

stories.title: WashU graduate programs see decline in international enrollment
stories.summary: International student enrollment in WashU master’s programs has fallen, with the total international graduate population dropping from 46.3 percent in 2023 to 38.2 percent by the tenth week of fall 2026. Undergraduate international enrollment has seen a slight increase over the same period, reaching 11.2 percent.

stories.title: Wellesley College pauses CPT for international students
stories.summary: Wellesley College has paused Curricular Practical Training authorization for international students on F-1 visas. Students report that the sudden change has cancelled off-campus plans and confined their professional opportunities to the campus. The college administration has not commented on the decision to bow to the regulations.

stories.title: Cavista and Babcock University partner for AI training
stories.summary: Cavista Technologies has signed an agreement with Babcock University to provide AI training and industry mentorship to students. The partnership includes a mini-curriculum designed to bridge the gap between classroom instruction and industry requirements. The company aims to prepare students for emerging global technology opportunities.

stories.title: Report finds AI use in classrooms lacks guidance
stories.summary: A survey of K-12 staff and parents shows over half of students use AI for schoolwork, primarily for writing and media generation. While students are told when to use these tools, most staff report a lack of time for proper training on how to use them.

stories.title: Atal Tinkering Labs reach 1.1 crore students
stories.summary: More than 10,000 Atal Tinkering Labs have been established across India to encourage students to explore robotics and AI. The initiative, part of the Atal Innovation Mission, aims to move learning beyond textbooks by providing hands-on innovation opportunities to over 1.1 crore students as of June 2026.

stories.title: SIU to host AI workshop for students and staff
stories.summary: Southern Illinois University Carbondale will host a workshop today on how AI is transforming career and research opportunities. Led by doctoral researcher Johnbosco Nnamso, the free session is open to all majors, faculty and staff. Refreshments will be provided for those who attend the 90-minute event.

stories.title: Nagaland considers expanding AI curriculum target
stories.summary: Nagaland is developing an AI curriculum under Mission SOAR for students starting in Class 6. The state is currently collecting student views on education reform and may increase its participation target from 1,000 to 2,500 students to better represent the aspirations of young people in the region.

stories.title: Karnataka to train 5,000 teachers in AI literacy
stories.summary: The government of Karnataka will train 5,000 public school teachers in AI literacy under the JanAI initiative. Announced by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, the 12-month programme aims to promote the responsible use of AI within the state education system starting in January 2027.

stories.title: Microsoft and Philippines education department partner on AI
stories.summary: Microsoft has launched a resource suite for Filipino teachers to earn AI credentials and access classroom tools. The programme, Microsoft Elevate for Educators, aims to help teachers guide students on privacy and critical thinking. The initiative focuses on equipping classrooms for the safe and responsible use of AI.

stories.title: Durham students launch platform to bypass AI job screening
stories.summary: A group of students has developed CVSuite.ai to help applicants improve their resumes against automated job screening systems. The platform provides data to careers teams to identify where students are being rejected by software. The project addresses the issue of generic AI content in job applications.

stories.title: NIIT University partners with Fractal for AI projects
stories.summary: NIIT University and Fractal have partnered to create an AI and Analytics Centre of Excellence. The collaboration will offer third-year students capstone projects in generative AI and agentic workflows. The centre aims to provide practical industry experience through technical guidance and project-based learning.

stories.title: Civics proficiency remains low in Australian schools
stories.summary: Only 28 percent of Year 10 students meet the proficient standard in civics and citizenship, the lowest level since testing began in 2004. Experts suggest that upcoming curriculum changes will require significant investment in teacher training and professional development to improve these results in the classroom.

stories.title: NIEPD reviews global teacher development trends
stories.summary: The National Institute for Educational Professional Development has reviewed the OECD Education at a Glance 2026 report. The briefing examined international shifts in teacher preparation and the sustainability of the workforce, aiming to apply global findings to local professional development strategies and educational policy.

stories.title: Karnataka government launches teacher AI training
stories.summary: Karnataka will train 5,000 government school teachers in AI literacy through the JanAI initiative. The 12-month programme, running throughout 2027, seeks to ensure that AI tools are adopted safely and meaningfully in classrooms. The project is coordinated with the Department of School Education and Literacy.

stories.title: Ghana Education Service completes promotion exercise
stories.summary: More than 60,000 teachers have completed the Ghana Education Service promotion exercise. The process, which separates professional ranks from administrative roles, was reported as smooth by monitoring officials. The policy is intended to expand career advancement opportunities for educators across the country.

stories.title: The role of English teachers in the age of AI
stories.summary: The rise of AI tools capable of correcting and translating language has created uncertainty for English teachers in Europe and India. The profession faces questions regarding how to adapt to technology that can perform many traditional classroom tasks, with demand for English instruction remaining at record highs.

stories.title: Educators debate the role of human connection in AI classrooms
stories.summary: As AI becomes capable of answering questions in seconds, educators are questioning the future of the teaching profession. Experts suggest that teachers must shift their focus from imparting knowledge to fostering character and human connection, as machines become increasingly efficient at performing traditional academic tasks.

stories.title: TSC reopens teacher appraisal portal after technical issues
stories.summary: The Teachers Service Commission has reopened its online appraisal portal following weeks of technical failures. Teachers had reported issues with log-ins and document uploads that prevented them from meeting submission deadlines. The system is now available again to allow staff to complete their pending performance appraisals.

stories.title: UIU hosts 20th teacher development conference
stories.summary: United International University hosted the 20th Teacher Development Conference on October 31. The event, organized with the Bangladesh English Language Teachers Association, focused on cultivating community in language education. The conference brought together international researchers and professionals to exchange pedagogical practices and strengthen collaboration.

stories.title: Teachers report mixed experiences with AI in classrooms
stories.summary: Educators are using AI to organize data, develop lesson plans and provide student feedback, according to reports from ABC News. While some teachers view the technology as a creative tool, others are seeking formal guidance on how to integrate AI into their daily instruction.

stories.summary: The Bihar government has banned teachers and students from uploading social media reels without permission. This follows a new formal dress code introduced in late October. The state currently manages over 76,000 government schools, a system that has recently drawn national attention for its operational challenges.

stories.summary: Google will disable its search engine and AI features for K-12 student accounts by default. The company says it is responding to schools asking for more control over AI usage. Administrators can manually re-enable these tools, provided they are comfortable with the company's current configuration.

The call was made in Abuja at a Technical Working Group

stories.title: Centre reviews campus equity rules
stories.summary: The Union government is considering a committee to review the 2026 University Grants Commission regulations on campus equity. The rules were designed to combat discrimination but faced protests from students who claimed the policy was one-sided. The government has requested more time to respond to the criticism.

stories.title: Google ties search to AI for students
stories.summary: Google is integrating AI into its search engine for elementary and secondary students. While school boards can choose to turn these tools on or off, the company has made the AI-boosted version the only option for those who wish to keep using the search engine within classroom apps.

stories.title: Keralam questions university appointment
stories.summary: The Keralam Higher Education department has asked the University of Calicut to explain the appointment of a pro-Vice-Chancellor. The department is investigating how the professor was relieved of his duties at an aided college and moved to the university position without obtaining prior government sanction.

stories.title: Vice-chancellor calls for university model shift
stories.summary: Cardiff University vice-chancellor Wendy Larner says the British higher education sector can no longer afford to maintain a scaled-up Oxbridge model. She argued that universities must rethink their operating models, as not every institution needs to replicate the structure of Oxford and Cambridge.

stories.title: J&K universities directed to design degrees
stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha has ordered universities to roll out a Design Your Degree programme within six months. The directive aims to move beyond policy announcements and ensure that higher education reforms in the Union Territory translate into measurable outcomes for students.

stories.title: Pune to open eight CBSE schools
stories.summary: The Maharashtra government has granted a no-objection certificate for the Pune Municipal Corporation to launch eight CBSE-affiliated schools. Starting in the 2027-28 academic year, the initiative is expected to provide English-medium education to approximately 17,000 students across the city.

stories.title: Oakridge Vizag ranked first in Andhra Pradesh
stories.summary: Oakridge International School, Visakhapatnam, has been ranked No. 9 in India and No. 1 in Andhra Pradesh in the EducationWorld India School Rankings 2026 to 27. The rankings evaluate 4,500 schools across 34 cities. The school is now officially a benchmark for excellence in the state.

stories.title: Oakridge Mohali secures top local ranking
stories.summary: Oakridge International School, Mohali, has secured the No. 1 position in its city in the EducationWorld India School Rankings 2026 to 27. The assessment drew on feedback from 10,000 parents and various educators. The school remains a leading institution in the region according to the survey.

stories.title: White Lotus International School hosts annual festival
stories.summary: White Lotus International School in Surat celebrated its annual function, titled Anandam, at the Sanjeev Kumar Auditorium. The event focused on India’s cultural heritage and artistic expression. The school also announced the opening of a new campus, Aster School, in the same city.

stories.title: SRM University-AP debuts in Asia rankings
stories.summary: SRM University-AP has secured the No. 1 position among universities in Andhra Pradesh in the QS World University Rankings: Asia 2027. The institution also placed among the top 25 private universities in India. The ranking evaluates research, teaching, and graduate employability for the first time.

stories.title: Chowgule International School opens admissions
stories.summary: Chowgule International School in Goa has opened admissions for the 2027 to 28 academic year. The school promotes an inquiry-led curriculum designed to foster critical thinking and holistic development. It aims to prepare students for a changing world through its specific approach to learning.

stories.title: IPS officer Anukriti Sharma receives efficiency medal
stories.summary: IPS officer Anukriti Sharma has been recommended for the Home Minister's Efficiency Medal 2026. Previously a NASA employee, she joined the 2020 batch of the Indian Police Service. She is currently serving as Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police in Gautam Buddha Nagar.

stories.title: NCERT adds finance chapters to Class 9 curriculum
stories.summary: The NCERT has introduced chapters on personal finance and entrepreneurship to the Class 9 Social Science textbook. Students will learn about mutual funds, taxes, and business plans. The curriculum change aims to familiarise students with financial decisions before they enter the workforce.

research.title: Preprimary education laws and women’s empowerment later in life
research.summary: Nature Human Behaviour, Published online: 04 November 2026, doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02608-z Across nearly 6.7 million women in 117 low- and middle-income countries, eligibility under national preprimary education laws was associated with higher educational enrolment and completion, more gender-egalitarian attitudes, more favourable empowerment-related behaviours and greater reproductive autonomy.

research.title: Preprimary education laws and women’s gender attitudes, empowerment and reproductive autonomy in 117 low- and middle-income countries
research.summary: Nature Human Behaviour, Published online: 04 November 2026, doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02583-5 Lou et al. find that eligibility for preprimary education is linked to more gender-equitable attitudes, greater empowerment and reproductive autonomy, and lower levels of adolescent marriage and childbearing across low- and middle-income countries.
